rv.q: Ms. Opdyke’s potentially moving story is handled in such a banal, ham-fisted manner that it sometimes feels like bad fiction.

There is at least one reason to be grateful that Irena's Vow has arrived on Broadway: After this production, it's doubtful that anyone will be itching to produce a stage adaptation of Schindler's List.
It's one of the single most dramatic moments in the production, which says an incriminating lot about the flatness of both Gordon's script and Michael Parva's direction.

""Irena’s Vow" may be melodramatic and occasionally manipulative, but the emotions this stage biography stirs in theatergoers are genuine, a testament to the bravery and tenacity of the woman whose real-life story is being told.
"A little-known story of heroism is transformed into theatrical hokum in “Irena’s Vow,” a play by Dan Gordon about a young Polish woman who helped a dozen Jews survive the Holocaust.

cn.t: Critics find this Holocaust drama about Polish hero Irena Gut Opdyke well-intentioned but dramatically flawed, criticizing it as manipulative theatrical hokum that exploits emotional territory rather than honoring it effectively.

sg.ra: Intimate 975-seat house with curved rows reducing angle loss. Rows D-H sit ahead of the mezzanine overhang (which starts at row H-J per TickPick/SeatPlan) and are past the stage-height issue reported at row B-C ('stage is high when sitting in the second row center orchestra, so you miss some upstage action' — Headout). JK's TheatreScene confirms Row J still delivers 'full view of the action' for Hadestown including turntables/elevators.

Most expensive rows in the theater. Delivers immersion but SeatPlan reviewer at C8 (6' tall) warns 'usual up-close view where you are looking up at the action,' and Headout echoes 'stage is high when sitting in the second row center orchestra, so you miss some upstage action.' For Hadestown's turntables and upstage balcony effects this is a real trade-off.

Sits fully under the mezzanine overhang (begins H-J) and the orchestra rake is notably shallow — AVFMS/SeatPlan reviewer at N116 explicitly calls out 'rake in the orchestra is not great,' meaning head-blocking from patrons in front is a real issue. Combined with the overhang cutting top-of-stage for Hadestown's upper balcony set, these seats underperform their price.

Rows curve toward stage per SeatPlan, mitigating the side-angle penalty. JK's TheatreScene (Oct 2025) bought J15 for Hadestown at $139, called it 'plenty of leg room' and praised full band visibility plus upstage action (turntable/elevator effects 'perfect from this perspective') because row J sits just ahead of the overhang. TickPick echoes: right side better for band and Hades' balcony visibility than left. Only isValuePick in this dataset.

Multiple sources converge: TickPick says Center Mezz 'promises some of the best views in the Walter Kerr Theatre for the show's visual effects and stage revolve'; SeatPlan confirms 'steep rake ensures patrons in front shouldn't block the view'; SeatPlan reviewer davidnewell (Row C, 5'10") reports 'view is fantastic since row in front is much lower.' Critical for Hadestown specifically because the show's vertical staging (Hades' balcony, revolve) reads best from elevated center.

TickPick explicitly flags Walter Kerr's side mezzanine as unusually strong: 'Unlike many Broadway theaters, the very sides of the Mezzanine are not obstructed.' SeatPlan confirms steep rake keeps sightlines clear, and TickPick recommends Right Mezzanine specifically for Hadestown band/Hades' balcony visibility. Genuine budget pick.

SeatPlan: 'mezzanine has a very steep rake, so most of the seats offer a clear view, but the rear section feels quite far away from the action.' Intimate house (975 cap) + steep rake means even back rows keep a clean unobstructed view per TickPick/SeatPlan, but the distance is real. Better bet for spectacle musicals than dialogue-dense plays.

Near-unanimous negative: TickPick quotes a patron calling it 'not a balcony, but rather the catwalk for the spotlights.' TripAdvisor (Gentleman's Guide): 'view was totally obstructed seeing the spot lights... stage was not totally visible without standing up.' SeatPlan: 'lighting rigs attached to the outside of the Balcony and the ceiling' create obstructions, 'B18 also has thin support pillars,' overhang starts at row D (cuts top of stage), and 'legroom at this height is cramped.' Only 68 seats, two rows — avoid unless deeply discounted and the show is vocals-forward.
